The dynamic between Elizabeth Bennet and Mr. Darcy serves as the primary vehicle for exploring the novel's themes of class and social mobility. Their initial relationship, characterized by mutual disdain rooted in Darcy's pride and Elizabeth's prejudice, illustrates the rigid barriers of the Regency era's social hierarchy. As they undergo personal growth—Darcy learning humility and Elizabeth recognizing her own misjudgments—their evolving bond demonstrates that genuine connection can transcend societal expectations. This transformation underscores the theme of self-reflection, suggesting that individual character is more significant than birthright, thereby challenging the static nature of class structures.
